1.x: Land grants in tribal frontiers brought **virgin land under cultivation**; post-Gupta **copper-plate charters describe various types of land**; the **Smritis** speak of graded rights in the same land – **Mahipati** (king), **Kshetrasvamin** (owner), **Karshaka** (cultivator) and **sub-tenant**.
The Pallava grants mention **18 types of taxes** exempted for donated villages.
**Early medieval features:** hierarchical **land intermediaries** with feudal titles and military obligations, prevalence of **vishti**, and a relatively **closed village economy**.

**Essential elements:** an administrative structure based on **control and possession of land**, and a **lord–vassal** relationship; a **strong central authority** with weak local power is the opposite of feudalism.
Post-Gupta **feudalism** arose because a **landowning intermediate class** and a **dependent peasantry** emerged.

2.x: **Kulyavapa / dronavapa:** **Units of land measurement** in Bengal inscriptions – area sown with one kulya / one drona of seed.

3.x: **Monarchy:** Gupta rule was hereditary **kingship** with divine claims; **primogeniture was not firm**.
**Titles:** **Maharajadhiraja, Parameshvara, Paramabhattaraka**; kings likened to **Vishnu**; **Samudragupta** equated with **Kubera (Dhanada), Varuna, Indra and Yama (Antaka)**.
**Decentralised:** unlike the Mauryas, much of the empire was held by **feudatories (samantas)** – **Samudragupta** reinstated defeated kings; officials were often paid in **land or kind**.

r: Most important officers, appointed by the king in the **home provinces**; ministers and commanders chosen from them

3.x: **Village headman:** became **more important** in Gupta times – **no land transaction could be effected without his consent**; **Mahattara and Pattakila** were his designations.

**Adhikarana (Kotivarsha, Damodarpur plates):** **Nagarashreshthi** (chair, chief banker), **Sarthavaha** (chief caravan trader), **Prathama kulika** (chief artisan), **Prathama kayastha** (chief scribe); a **district council** helped the district officer.

**Law:** civil and criminal law first clearly demarcated – **property disputes = civil**, theft and adultery = criminal; **Narada smriti** (survives complete, civil law), Brihaspati and Katyayana (fragments).
